issues.note: Modal must takes the bare infinitive; to-infinitive pattern is wrong.
Abbreviation e.g. is forbidden in prose; write for example.
Must not is the negative of sense 1, not a separate sense; an example would help.
Same wrong to-infinitive pattern, contradicting the examples and the learner error.
Shall for obligation is formal or legal only; misleading as a plain synonym.
The have to contrast is already stated in the sense explanation.
Forbidden and not necessary are different meanings, not opposites.
Both see_also items duplicate the compare list and restate it.
The no-past fact appears in four fields; one fact belongs in one field.
Repeats the inaccurate opposite claim and other facts stated elsewhere.
The cannot-as-opposite fact is stated in the explanation, compare, and adaptation.
This is an obligation example placed under the deduction sense.
Phrase explanation only restates the definition.
Must has no past form; must have is a different structure, but scoping it would help.
Obligation example does not fit the almost-certainly-true sense.
This is the third statement of the cannot fact.
I must say and I must admit are frequent and not covered.

findings.F1: Sense 1 pattern 'verb + to-infinitive' is wrong for a modal and contradicts the other fields.
findings.F2: The usage note uses the abbreviation 'e.g.'.
findings.F3: shall-modal is listed as a synonym of obligation must without any formal or legal restriction.
findings.F4: The have-to compare note restates the sense 1 explanation.
findings.F5: Must not and do not have to are called 'opposite'; they differ in meaning but are not opposites.
findings.F6: see_also duplicates the sense 1 compare items.
findings.F7: The no-past fact and the must not / don't have to contrast are repeated across several fields.
findings.F8: The cannot-as-opposite-of-deduction fact is stated three times.
findings.F9: An obligation example is placed under sense 2 (almost certainly true).
findings.F10: The 'if you must' phrase explanation only restates its definition.
findings.F11: The emphasizing use 'I must say' / 'I must admit' is not covered.

missed: The common recommendation or insistent invitation use (You must try this cake; You must come and visit) is not shown in any sense or example.
